RE: SUPPORT for LD 1158 An Act to Expand Appliance Energy and Water Standards
Dear Chair Tepler, Vice-Chair Doudera, and Members of the Environment & Natural Resources Committee:
Please accept this testimony from the Appliance Standards Awareness Project (ASAP) in support of LD 1158. ASAP is a project of the American Council for an Energy Efficient Economy (ACEEE) and works to advance cost-effective appliance standards at the national and state level.
Our organization, along with ACEEE, published States Go First, a report outlining recommendations for state-level appliance efficiency standards.1 We also publish and annually update state savings estimates for the adoption of efficiency standards. We would be happy to provide additional information about the products, standards, and analysis used to inform LD 1185 as requested.
In 2021, Maine adopted efficiency standards for 10 products to help residents and businesses save money on utility bills while also cutting harmful air pollutants, including carbon dioxide.2 Today, LD 1158 seeks to expand the list of covered products to further increase the money saved and air pollutants avoided.
FACTS ABOUT LD 1158:
� Very cost effective to buyers and users -All of the proposed standards save money on utility bills for consumers and businesses purchasing the products.
� Readily available - Products and technologies meeting the standards are readily available today from multiple manufacturers.
� Reduce strain on electric grid - The standards help reduce demand on the electric grid, including during peak demand hours.
LD 1158 WOULD SAVE MONEY, ENERGY, AND REDUCE GREENHOUSE GASES
The bill would set minimum energy or water efficiency standards for nine products. If adopted, ASAP estimates the standards could save Maine residents and businesses about $3 million on utility bills in 2030.3 As more and more efficient products are purchased, annual utility bill savings would grow, reaching $9 million in 2040. In total, by 2050, the standards would save $169 million on utility bills, money that stays in local communities and can be reinvested in the local economy.
The standards in LD 1158 are also estimated to save 298 gigawatt hours of electricity and 320,000 metric tons of CO2 by 2050, or the equivalent of taking about 74,000 cars off the road for a year.
1 ASAP/ACEEE report: States Go First: How States Can Save consumers Money, Reduce Energy and Water Waste, and Protect the Environment with New Appliance Standards. 2 LD 940. 3 See 2025 Maine Appliance Standards Savings Report on the ASAP website or the report is copied below.

STATES IN THE REGION AND NATIONWIDE CONTINUE TO ADOPT STANDARDS
In recent years, 12 other states have adopted efficiency standards like those found in LD 1158. This includes in the northeast, Vermont, Massachusetts, New York, and Rhode Island. Nationwide, Nevada, Colorado, New Jersey, Maryland, Washington, Oregon, California, and Hawaii have also adopted product efficiency standards. If efficiency standards are not adopted, the state could become the dumping ground for the less efficient products that can no longer be sold in these states, saddling consumers and businesses with higher utility bills.
EXISTING PRODUCTS NOT IMPACTED
Additionally, products would not have to proactively changed out because of HB 660. The bill only applies to new sales of new products. Consumers could continue to use their existing products as long as they wish. The bill just means that after the effective date it will be the more efficient products available for purchase. The bill also does not apply to the sales of used products.
COMPLIANCE DATE NEARLY TWO YEARS AWAY
If adopted, the standards would go into effect on January 1, 2027. Distributors and retailers will have more than 18 months to sell noncompliant products before the standards take effect.
STANDARDS ARE A COST-EFFECTIVE WAY TO ACHIEVE STATE GOALS
Adopting efficiency standards is a low-cost way for Maine to cut energy and water waste, reduce utility bills and reduce greenhouse gases - the latter helping the state meet Maine's climate goals.
We would be happy to provide further information, answer questions, or provide technical assistance should the need arise.
Thank you,
Brian Fadie State Policy Manager Appliance Standards Awareness Project

in Support of HP 763/LD 1158: An Act to Expand Appliance Energy and Water Standards
April 4, 2025
Senator Denise Tepler, Representative Victoria Doudera, and members of the Committee on Environment and Natural Resources:
My name is Courtney Griffin, and I am the Director of Consumer Product Safety for the Consumer Federation of America (CFA). Founded in 1968, CFA is one of the nation's largest consumer organizations working in the consumer interest through research, advocacy and education. CFA represents over 200 national, state and local groups. For more than 20 years, CFA has supported and promoted cost-effective energy and water efficiency policies and practices at the federal, state and local levels. I am submitting testimony on behalf of CFA in strong support of HP 763/LD 1158, "An Act to Expand Appliance Energy and Water Standards." This bill represents a crucial step towards a more sustainable and cost-effective future for Maine residents.
HP 763/LD 1158's numerous benefits to consumers include:
1. Lower energy costs. By updating energy efficiency standards for appliances, this bill will help reduce energy consumption, leading to lower utility bills for households across Maine. The Appliance Standards Awareness Project estimates that the potential annual utility bill savings in Maine for commercial battery chargers, commercial dishwashers, commercial fryers, commercial ovens, commercial steam cookers, gas fireplaces, residential ventilating fans, and server power supplies will total $69 million in 2030 through 2050.
2. Environmental and public health benefits. Appliance standards enhance the efficiency of both residential and commercial products, leading to energy savings. This helps lower climate-changing emissions and reduces other environmental impacts linked to the production, distribution, and use of electricity, natural gas, and other fuels. Additionally, it helps conserve fresh water supplies, easing the strain caused by both short- and long-term droughts.

As a consumer group, we support HP 763/LD 1158 because it will reduce energy consumption and address the pressing need for energy affordability. We urge you to support the legislation to ensure a more energy-efficient, cost-effective, and sustainable future for all Maine residents.
Thank you for your consideration.
Courtney Griffin Director of Consumer Product Safety Consumer Federation of America cgriffin@consumerfed.org

Testimony in Support of LD 1158, An Act to Expand Appliance Energy and Water
Standards
To the Committee on Environment and Natural Resources
by Sarah Nichols, NRCM
April 7, 2025
Senator Tepler, Representative Doudera, members of the Environment and Natural Resources
Committee, my name is Sarah Nichols, and I'm here today to testify in support of LD 1158, An
Act to Expand Appliance Energy and Water Standards on behalf of the Natural Resources
Council of Maine (NRCM). NRCM is Maine's leading nonprofit, nonpartisan enviromnental
advocacy organization with 20,000 members and supporters statewide.
This bill would expand the list of appliances covered under Maine's appliance efficiency
standard established in 2021. NRCM supported the establishment of appliance efficiency
standards in Maine to ensure that the appliances We purchase use energy and water more
efficiently while preserving quality and affordability. Thirteen states have enacted appliance standards since 2018, including Maine, which adopted standards for 10 products in 2021. Without standards, Maine risks becoming a dumping ground for inefficient products.
In setting these requirements, Maine households and businesses will not only aid in achieving a marked reduction in the state's carbon and other pollutants but will also benefit from an improvement in the usefulness of the covered appliances and from a reduction in utility bills. In fact, if the proposed standards are enacted, Maine consumers and businesses would see $169 million in utility bill savings by 2050.`
